text: WHEN system initialization begins, the software shall execute the Power-On Built-In Test before enabling application outputs.
WHILE the Power-On Built-In Test is active, the software shall verify volatile memory using the configured memory-test sequence.
WHILE the Power-On Built-In Test is active, the software shall verify processor health using the configured processor self-test.
WHEN configuration data is loaded during initialization, the software shall verify its integrity using the stored checksum and schema identifier.
WHEN every mandatory startup test completes successfully, the software shall declare the Power-On Built-In Test result as PASS.
WHEN a mandatory startup test fails or exceeds its completion timeout, the software shall declare the Power-On Built-In Test result as FAIL.
WHILE the system is in an operational state, the software shall execute the Continuous Built-In Test once per health-monitoring cycle.
WHILE Continuous Built-In Test is active, the software shall assess each safety-significant sensor for freshness, range, validity, and plausibility.
WHILE actuator commands are enabled, the software shall compare commanded actuator state with qualified position or current feedback.
WHEN the communication supervision timer expires without a valid frame, the software shall identify the associated external interface as unavailable.
WHEN the age of a required sample exceeds its source-specific freshness threshold, the software shall classify the sample as stale.
WHEN a monitored parameter violates its configured boundary for the persistence interval, the software shall identify an out-of-range condition.
WHEN a protected arithmetic operation exceeds the representable numeric range, the software shall record an arithmetic-overflow fault.
WHEN a divisor magnitude is below the configured minimum, the software shall prevent the division operation and record a divide-by-zero fault.
The software shall maintain a bit-mapped Built-In Test summary containing the severity and confirmation state of every monitored test.
The software shall maintain an independent status indication for each detectable failure mode without clearing unrelated indications.
WHEN a suspected fault becomes confirmed, the software shall timestamp the confirmation using the monotonic system time.
WHEN a fault becomes active, the software shall log its code, operating mode, confirmation basis, and relevant snapshot data.
WHEN confirmed recovery evidence remains valid for the complete clearing interval, the software shall log the corresponding fault-clear event.
WHEN the Built-In Test reporting interval expires or critical status changes, the software shall publish the current test result to external interfaces.
WHERE initiated maintenance testing is supported, the software shall start Initiated Built-In Test following an authenticated command in a permitted state.
WHEN Initiated Built-In Test terminates, the software shall report completed, aborted, passed, failed, or inconclusive status.
WHILE actuation is active, a safety transition is pending, or execution margin is insufficient, the software shall inhibit Initiated Built-In Test.
WHEN a fault becomes confirmed, the software shall classify it using the configured safety classification and failure-effect criteria.
WHEN a critical fault becomes confirmed, the software shall enter fail-safe mode within the same processing cycle.
WHEN a sensor sample is received, the software shall qualify its validity before admission to the current-cycle monitored data set.
WHEN redundant qualified measurements exceed the mode-dependent disagreement tolerance for the persistence interval, the software shall declare sensor disagreement.
WHILE an actuator is commanded, the software shall evaluate feedback validity using qualified position, current, and communication evidence.
WHILE the system is operational, the software shall calculate processor utilization over the configured averaging window excluding idle and startup intervals.
WHEN task completion exceeds its allocated execution budget for the configured number of cycles, the software shall declare a task-overrun condition.
WHEN the watchdog service deadline is missed or a watchdog reset cause is detected, the software shall declare a watchdog-timeout event.
WHEN controlled initialization begins, the software shall reset transient fault counters without altering retained maintenance history.
WHEN a confirmed fault occurrence is recorded, the software shall increment its saturating cumulative occurrence counter.
WHEN valid recovery evidence satisfies the configured hysteresis and duration criteria, the software shall clear the associated transient fault.
WHILE a critical fault remains latched, the software shall retain its indication until an authorized reset is accepted after the initiating condition is absent.
WHEN the health-reporting interval expires, the software shall generate a coherent snapshot of mode, Built-In Test summary, active faults, and resource status.
WHEN a confirmed fault permits continued operation with approved limitations, the software shall indicate degraded-mode operation.
WHEN a maintenance-significant fault activates, clears, or changes severity, the software shall report the transition to the maintenance interface.
WHEN sufficient diagnostic evidence is available, the software shall isolate the confirmed fault to the lowest supported replaceable or diagnosable subsystem.
WHEN fault-history storage reaches its configured capacity, the software shall remove the oldest non-latched entry before storing the new event.
WHEN a control cycle begins, the software shall calculate control error from the selected reference and qualified feedback for the active mode.
WHEN the periodic control trigger occurs, the software shall execute one non-overlapping instance of the control algorithm.
WHEN sensor qualification completes, the software shall admit only valid, fresh, in-range, and source-consistent measurements to control calculations.
WHEN an input sample fails qualification, the software shall exclude it from control-state updates and record the rejection reason.
WHEN a non-critical input becomes invalid and a mode-specific substitute is configured, the software shall apply the substitute and indicate substitution.
WHEN qualified control error is available, the software shall calculate the proportional contribution using the scheduled gain for the operating point.
WHEN the integration step is due, the software shall calculate the integral contribution from accumulated qualified error and the configured sample interval.
WHEN filtered error change is available, the software shall calculate the derivative contribution using the configured time constant and noise-limiting filter.
WHEN proportional, integral, and derivative contributions are available, the software shall combine their independently limited values into a preliminary command.
WHEN the active operating mode changes, the software shall select the validated control-gain set associated with the new mode.
WHEN the unsaturated and applied commands indicate further integrator windup, the software shall constrain the integral state using the configured anti-windup method.
WHEN a preliminary command exceeds the directional slew constraint, the software shall limit its change to the applicable rate boundary.
WHEN control-law computation completes, the software shall constrain the preliminary command to the configured output saturation limits.
WHILE a command value is propagated through the control path, the software shall enforce the applicable lower and upper numeric boundaries.
WHEN an approved gain-scheduling boundary is reached, the software shall activate the validated gain set after continuity checks pass.
WHERE controller tuning is configurable, the software shall maintain parameter units, ranges, defaults, and compatibility metadata in the controlled parameter set.
WHEN a validated parameter update reaches a control-cycle boundary, the software shall activate the complete authorized parameter set atomically.
WHEN controller parameters are initialized or updated, the software shall verify their signature, version, length, range, and schema compatibility.
WHEN control processing initializes, the software shall set controller states to mode-specific values that avoid an uncontrolled command discontinuity.
WHEN an authorized controller-reset command is accepted, the software shall reset controller states to bumpless values consistent with current reference and feedback.
WHEN successful initialization completes without an enable authorization, the software shall enter STANDBY as the default non-actuating mode.
WHEN control prerequisites and output authorization become valid, the software shall make ACTIVE mode available for transition.
WHEN continued control is permitted with approved functional limitations, the software shall make DEGRADED mode available for transition.
WHEN a confirmed critical condition requires safe behavior, the software shall make FAIL-SAFE mode the highest-priority transition target.
WHEN an enable command is authorized and all activation guards are satisfied, the software shall transition from STANDBY to ACTIVE.
WHEN a confirmed non-critical fault maps to an approved degraded capability, the software shall transition to DEGRADED mode.
WHEN a confirmed critical fault requires safe operation, the software shall transition to FAIL-SAFE ahead of non-safety transition requests.
WHEN a mode transition completes, the software shall record the previous mode, new mode, initiating event, result, and monotonic timestamp.
WHEN a requested mode transition violates authorization or guard criteria, the software shall reject the request and retain the current mode.
The software shall provide one authoritative operating-mode indication consistent with all completed state entry and exit actions.
WHEN control computation and authorization gating complete, the software shall generate the cycle output command from the accepted control result.
WHEN an output command is generated, the software shall qualify it for range, rate, freshness, numeric validity, and mode consistency before transmission.
WHILE the system is in FAIL-SAFE mode, the software shall inhibit every output not explicitly permitted by the safety-output configuration.
WHILE FAIL-SAFE operation is active, the software shall command the mode-specific safe-state values without dependence on an unqualified control result.
WHEN an output command is released, the software shall publish its classification as valid, substituted, held, inhibited, or safe-state.
WHEN an unconstrained command reaches a configured magnitude or directional boundary, the software shall report command saturation.
WHEN the output interface deadline approaches, the software shall complete the corresponding command update within the allocated cycle time.
WHILE command tracking is enabled, the software shall compare qualified feedback with the delayed commanded response over the configured observation window.
WHEN qualified command and feedback data are available, the software shall calculate absolute, signed, and accumulated output-error metrics.
WHEN required command generation, qualification, authorization, or transmission does not complete, the software shall flag an output-generation failure.
WHILE an operational control mode is active, the software shall execute the control algorithm at the mode-defined periodic rate without concurrent instances.
WHEN a control cycle begins, the software shall complete all control calculations before the cycle output-update deadline.
WHEN consecutive control-cycle starts are observed, the software shall calculate cycle duration using the monotonic system clock.
WHEN cycle duration exceeds its budget by the configured tolerance and persistence count, the software shall report a cycle overrun.
WHILE the system is operational, the software shall monitor average and peak processor utilization over the configured observation window.
WHEN a control cycle starts, the software shall calculate loop jitter as deviation from the scheduled periodic release time.
The software shall maintain deterministic control execution through bounded completion time, fixed operation ordering, and mode-defined data dependencies.
WHEN a qualified system-time update is accepted, the software shall synchronize time-dependent functions without propagating discontinuities from external wall-clock time.
WHEN configuration parameters are committed, the software shall store them in non-volatile memory with integrity metadata, version information, and atomic replacement.
WHEN startup configuration data becomes available, the software shall validate it before dependent functions access the data or operational outputs are enabled.
WHEN checksum, signature, schema, range, or cross-parameter consistency verification fails, the software shall reject the affected configuration data set.
WHEN an authorized recovery command is accepted and the protected default set passes validation, the software shall restore factory-default parameters atomically.
WHEN an approved configuration change is committed, the software shall update configuration-version information for compatibility assessment.
The software shall provide software-build version information from immutable metadata associated with the executing image.
WHEN the periodic health-reporting interval expires, the software shall generate a coherent message from qualified health information.
WHEN an authenticated diagnostic request is accepted, the software shall generate the requested report without blocking safety-critical cyclic processing.
WHEN active-fault information is requested, the software shall report identifier, severity, status, occurrence count, and transition timestamps.
WHEN controller status is requested, the software shall report active mode, execution status, limiting state, substitution state, and parameter-set version.
WHEN operating-mode status is requested, the software shall report the authoritative state-machine result and the cause of the latest completed transition.
WHEN overall Built-In Test status is requested, the software shall report passed, failed, degraded, in-progress, or inconclusive from qualified test evidence.
